title.zh: 卷五十五 列傳第十五 臧燾 徐廣 傅隆
title.en: Volume 55 Biographies 15: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, F Long
title.raw: 卷五十五 列傳第十五 臧燾 徐廣 傅隆 Volume 55 Biographies 15: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, F Long

sentences.zh: 列傳第十五 臧燾徐廣傅隆

translations.literal: Biography 15: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, Fu Long
translations.idiomatic: Biography 15 — Zang Dao, Xu Guang, and Fu Long

sentences.zh: 臧燾，字德仁，東莞莒人，武敬皇后兄也。

translations.literal: Zang Dao, styled De Ren, was a man of Ju in Dongguan and elder brother to Empress Wu Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Dao, whose courtesy name was De Ren, came from Ju in Dongguan and was the elder brother of Empress Wu Jing.

sentences.zh: 少好學，善《三禮》，貧約自立，操行為鄉里所稱。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, was skilled in the Three Rites, supported himself in poverty and frugality, and his conduct was praised in his district.
translations.idiomatic: From an early age he devoted himself to study and excelled in the Three Rites. Though poor, he made his own way, and his moral bearing won praise throughout his home district.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元中，衛將軍謝安始立國學，徐、兗二州刺史謝玄舉燾為助教。

translations.literal: In the Taixuan era of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, Defender-General Xie An first established the National Academy, and Xie Xuan, regional inspector of Xu and Yan, recommended Dao as assistant instructor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taixuan reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, Defender-General Xie An founded the National Academy for the first time, and Xie Xuan, inspector of Xu and Yan, recommended Dao to serve as an assistant instructor.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝追崇庶祖母宣太后，議者或謂宜配食中宗。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu posthumously honored his father's concubine mother, Empress Dowager Xuan, and some in the debate held that she should receive offerings alongside Emperor Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu raised his father's concubine mother, Empress Dowager Xuan, to posthumous honor, some debaters argued that she ought to share sacrificial offerings in the temple of Emperor Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 燾議曰：「《陽秋》，之義，母以子貴，故仲子、成風，咸稱夫人。

translations.literal: Dao submitted a memorial saying: "The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that a mother is ennobled through her son; therefore Zhong Zi and Cheng Feng were both styled Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Dao argued in a memorial: "According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, a mother is elevated through her son's rank; that is why Zhong Zi and Cheng Feng were both addressed as Lady.

sentences.zh: 《經》雲'考仲子之宮'。

translations.literal: The Classic says, 'Inspect the temple of Zhong Zi.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic states, 'Inspect the temple of Zhong Zi.'

sentences.zh: 若配食惠廟，則宮無緣別築。

translations.literal: If she were to share offerings in the temple of Emperor Hui, there would be no reason to build a separate temple.
translations.idiomatic: If she were given a place in Emperor Hui's temple, there would be no occasion to erect a separate shrine.

sentences.zh: 前漢孝文、孝昭太后，並系子為號，祭於寢園，不配于高祖、孝武之廟。

translations.literal: The empress dowagers Wen and Zhao of Former Han both took titles derived from their sons, were sacrificed to in the park shrines at their tombs, and were not paired in the temples of Gaozu and Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In Former Han, the empress dowagers Wen and Zhao both bore titles tied to their sons, received sacrifice in the tomb-park shrines, and were not installed as consorts in the temples of Gaozu and Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 後漢和帝之母曰恭懷皇所，安帝祖母曰敬隱皇后，順帝之母曰恭湣皇后，雖不系子為號，亦祭於陵寢。

translations.literal: In Later Han, the mother of Emperor He was called Empress Gonghuai, the grandmother of Emperor An was called Empress Jingyin, and the mother of Emperor Shun was called Empress Gongmin; though their titles were not derived from their sons, they too were sacrificed to at the tomb shrines.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han, Emperor He's mother was known as Empress Gonghuai, Emperor An's grandmother as Empress Jingyin, and Emperor Shun's mother as Empress Gongmin; although their titles were not framed through their sons' reign names, they likewise received sacrifice at the tomb shrines.

sentences.zh: 不配章、安二帝。

translations.literal: They were not paired with Emperors Zhang and An.
translations.idiomatic: None of them was paired with the temples of Emperors Zhang and An.

sentences.zh: 此則二漢雖有太后、皇后之異，至於並不配食，義同《陽秋》。

translations.literal: Thus although the two Han differed as to empress dowager and empress, in neither case were they given shared offerings, in the same sense as the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, although Former and Later Han differed in whether the women were styled empress dowager or empress, in neither dynasty were they given shared temple offerings — a principle in keeping with the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 唯光武追廢呂後，故以薄後配高祖廟。

translations.literal: Only Guangwu, in posthumously deposing Empress Lü, therefore paired Empress Bo in the temple of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Only under Guangwu, who posthumously deposed Empress Lü, was Empress Bo installed as consort in Gaozu's temple.

sentences.zh: 又衛後既廢，霍光追尊李夫人為皇后，配孝武廟，此非母以子貴之例，直以高、武二廟無配故耳。

translations.literal: Again, after Empress Wei was deposed, Huo Guang posthumously honored Lady Li as empress and paired her in the temple of Emperor Wu; this was not a case of a mother ennobled through her son, but simply because the temples of Gaozu and Emperor Wu lacked consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Again, after Empress Wei was deposed, Huo Guang posthumously honored Lady Li as empress and paired her with Emperor Wu's temple; that was not an instance of a mother elevated through her son, but merely because the temples of Gaozu and Emperor Wu had lacked consorts.

sentences.zh: 夫漢立寢於陵，自是晉制所異。

translations.literal: That Han established tomb shrines at the mausoleums was itself something Jin institutions differed from.
translations.idiomatic: Han practice of erecting tomb shrines at the mausoleums was in any case unlike Jin custom.

sentences.zh: 謂宜遠准《陽秋》考宮之義，近摹二漢不配之典。

translations.literal: I hold that one should take as distant standard the Annals' meaning of inspecting the temple, and as near model the two Han precedent of not pairing offerings.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that we should take as our distant standard the Annals' principle of the separate temple, and as our near precedent the two Han rule against shared offerings.

sentences.zh: 尊號既正，則罔極之情申，別建寢廟，則嚴禰之義顯，系子為稱，兼明母貴之所由，一舉而允三義，固哲王之高致也。」

translations.literal: Once the honorific title is correct, boundless filial feeling is expressed; if a separate tomb shrine is built, the solemn meaning of ancestral sacrifice is displayed; taking the son's name in the title also clarifies whence the mother's nobility derives — one act satisfying three principles is indeed the lofty aim of a sage king."
translations.idiomatic: Once her title is properly fixed, the fullest measure of filial devotion is expressed; if a separate shrine is built, the solemn dignity of ancestral worship is preserved; and framing her title through her son's name makes clear the source of her elevation — to satisfy all three principles in a single measure is truly the mark of a sage ruler."

sentences.zh: 議者從之。

translations.literal: The debaters followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly adopted his view.

sentences.zh: 頃之，去官。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he resigned his post.

sentences.zh: 以母老家貧，與弟熹俱棄人事，躬耕自業，約己養親者十餘載。

translations.literal: Because his mother was aged and his family poor, he and his younger brother Xi together abandoned worldly affairs, tilled the fields themselves to make their living, and for more than ten years restrained themselves to support their kin.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was old and the family poor, so he and his younger brother Xi withdrew from public life, worked the fields with their own hands, and for more than ten years lived frugally to support their parents.

sentences.zh: 父母喪亡，居喪六年，以毀瘠著稱。

translations.literal: When his parents died he observed mourning for six years and became renowned for emaciation from grief.
translations.idiomatic: After his parents died he mourned for six years and became famous for the wasting grief that marked his observance.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除臨沂令。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed magistrate of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, he was appointed magistrate of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 義旗建，為太學博士，參右將軍何無忌軍事，隨府轉鎮南參軍。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was raised he became erudite of the Imperial Academy, served as aide on military affairs to General of the Right He Wuji, and followed the headquarters to become aide of the Army of the South.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous armies rose, he was made an erudite of the Imperial Academy, joined General of the Right He Wuji's staff as military aide, and was later transferred with the headquarters to serve as aide of the Army of the South.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮京口，與燾書曰：「頃學尚廢弛，後進頹業，衡門之內，清風輟響。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor was stationed at Jingkou he wrote to Dao: "Recently learning has been neglected and slack, the younger generation's pursuit of study has declined, and within humble doorways the sound of pure conduct has ceased.
translations.idiomatic: While stationed at Jingkou, the Founding Emperor wrote to Dao: "Learning has lately fallen into neglect, the younger generation's devotion to study has waned, and within humble households the voice of upright conduct has fallen silent.

sentences.zh: 良由戎車屢警，禮樂中息，浮夫恣志，情與事染，豈可不敷崇墳籍，敦厲風尚。

translations.literal: Truly because war-chariots have repeatedly sounded the alarm and rites and music have halted midway, drifting men indulge their wills and sentiment is stained by affairs — how can we fail to spread reverence for the classics and urge refinement of custom?
translations.idiomatic: This is surely because war has repeatedly broken out, rites and music have been interrupted, and restless men follow their whims until feeling is corrupted by circumstance — how can we fail to promote the classics and strengthen public morals?

sentences.zh: 此境人士，子侄如林，明發搜訪，想聞令軌。

translations.literal: Men of talent in this region are as numerous as trees in a grove; at dawn I shall search them out, and I trust I shall hear of worthy models.
translations.idiomatic: Talented men in this region are as plentiful as trees in a forest; I intend to seek them out at once and hope to hear of exemplary conduct among them.

sentences.zh: 然荊玉含寶，要俟開瑩，幽蘭懷馨，事資扇發，獨習寡悟，義著周典。

translations.literal: Yet jade from Jing holds its treasure and must await polishing; orchids in the shade bear fragrance and depend on being fanned into bloom; solitary study yields little understanding — the principle is set forth in the Zhou canon.
translations.idiomatic: Yet jade from Jing hides its luster until it is cut and polished, and orchids in the shade need stirring to release their fragrance; solitary study brings little enlightenment — the Zhou classics themselves teach as much.

sentences.zh: 今經師不遠，而赴業無聞，非唯志學者鮮，或是勸誘未至邪。

translations.literal: Now masters of the classics are not far away, yet no word is heard of students coming to study — is it not only that those who wish to learn are few, or perhaps encouragement has not yet reached them?
translations.idiomatic: Masters of the classics are close at hand, yet we hear nothing of students flocking to study — is it only that aspiring scholars are few, or perhaps that encouragement has not yet been offered?

sentences.zh: 想複弘之。」

translations.literal: I trust you will again extend this effort."
translations.idiomatic: I trust you will take up this cause again."

sentences.zh: 參高祖中軍軍事，入補尚書度支郎，改掌祠部。

translations.literal: He joined the Founding Emperor's central army as military aide, entered the capital to fill the post of Director of Revenue in the Secretariat, and was reassigned to head the Sacrifices Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He then served on the Founding Emperor's central army staff as military aide, entered the capital as Director of Revenue in the Secretariat, and was later transferred to head the Sacrifices Bureau.

sentences.zh: 襲封高陵亭侯。

translations.literal: He inherited enfeoffment as Marquis of Gaoling district.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title Marquis of Gaoling district.

sentences.zh: 時太廟鴟尾災，燾謂著作郎徐廣曰：「昔孔子在齊，聞魯廟災，曰必桓、僖也。

translations.literal: At that time the temple finials of the Imperial Ancestral Temple caught fire; Dao said to Xu Guang, Master of Writings: "Formerly when Confucius was in Qi and heard of fire in the Lu temple, he said it must concern Huan and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When fire broke out at the finials of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Dao said to Xu Guang of the Master of Writings office: "Long ago, when Confucius was in Qi and heard that Lu's ancestral temple had burned, he said the disaster must concern the shrines of Duke Huan and Duke Xi.

sentences.zh: 今征西、京兆四府君，宜在毀落，而猶列廟饗，此其征乎？」

translations.literal: Now the four lords of the Western Campaign and Jingzhao offices ought to be among those removed, yet they still stand in the temple for sacrifice — is this not the omen?"
translations.idiomatic: Today the four ancestral lords of the Western Campaign and Jingzhao offices ought already to have been removed, yet they still receive temple sacrifice — is this not the same kind of sign?"

sentences.zh: 乃上議曰：「臣聞國之大事，在祀與戎，將營宮室，宗廟為首。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that the great affairs of a state are sacrifice and war; when palace buildings are to be planned, the ancestral temple comes first.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial: "I have heard that the great affairs of a state are sacrifice and war, and that when palaces are to be built, the ancestral temple must come first.

sentences.zh: 古先哲王，莫不致肅恭之誠心，盡崇嚴乎祖考，然後能流淳化于四海，通幽感於神明。

translations.literal: The sage kings of antiquity all devoted reverent and sincere hearts and showed the utmost honor to their forefathers, and only then could pure transformation flow through the four seas and hidden feeling reach the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of antiquity all brought reverent sincerity to their rites and showed the utmost honor to their ancestors; only then could pure teaching spread through the realm and the unseen world respond to their devotion.

sentences.zh: 固宜詳廢興於古典，循情禮以求中者也。

translations.literal: One should indeed examine abolition and establishment in the ancient canon and follow sentiment and ritual to seek the mean.
translations.idiomatic: One ought therefore to weigh abolition and establishment against the ancient canon and seek the mean in light of ritual and human feeling.

sentences.zh: 禮，天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖而七。

translations.literal: Ritual prescribes seven temples for the Son of Heaven: three zhao and three mu, with the Great Ancestor making seven.
translations.idiomatic: According to ritual, the Son of Heaven keeps seven temples — three zhao and three mu, with the Great Ancestor, for a total of seven.

sentences.zh: 自考廟以至祖考五廟，皆月祭之，遠廟為祧，有二祧，享嘗乃止。

translations.literal: From the temple of the father down to the five temples of the ancestors, all receive monthly sacrifice; distant temples become tiao, and when there are two tiao, only the seasonal offerings continue.
translations.idiomatic: From the temple of the immediate forebear down through the five temples of more distant ancestors, all receive monthly sacrifice; the most remote temples become tiao, and once there are two tiao, only the seasonal offerings remain.

sentences.zh: 去祧為壇，去壇為墠，有禱然後祭之。

translations.literal: When the tiao are removed they become altars; when the altars are removed they become open mounds; sacrifice is made only when there is prayer.
translations.idiomatic: When the tiao are removed they become altars; when the altars are removed they become open ritual mounds; and sacrifice is offered only when prayer is required.

sentences.zh: 此宗廟之次，親疏之序也。

translations.literal: This is the order of the ancestral temples and the sequence of near and remote kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the order of the ancestral temples and the gradation of kinship from near to remote.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄以為祧者文王、武王之廟，王肅以為五世六世之祖。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan held that the tiao were the temples of King Wen and King Wu; Wang Su held that they were ancestors of the fifth and sixth generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan held that the tiao were the temples of Kings Wen and Wu, whereas Wang Su held that they were ancestors of the fifth and sixth generations.

sentences.zh: 尋去祧之言，則祧非文、武之廟矣。

translations.literal: Examining the phrase 'removing the tiao,' the tiao cannot be the temples of Wen and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: If we examine the phrase 'removing the tiao,' the tiao cannot be the temples of Wen and Wu.

sentences.zh: 文、武周之祖宗，何雲去祧為壇乎？

translations.literal: Wen and Wu were the founding ancestors of Zhou — how could one speak of removing the tiao to make altars?
translations.idiomatic: Wen and Wu were Zhou's founding ancestors — how could the rites speak of removing the tiao to make altars?

sentences.zh: 明遠廟為祧者，無服之祖也。

translations.literal: This shows that distant temples made tiao are ancestors beyond the scope of mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: This makes clear that temples made tiao are ancestors beyond the range of mourning obligation.

sentences.zh: 又遠廟則有享嘗之禮，去祧則有壇墠之殊，明世遠者，其義彌疏也。

translations.literal: Again, distant temples still have the seasonal offering rites, while removed tiao have the distinction of altars and mounds — showing that the more remote the generation, the more attenuated the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, distant temples still receive seasonal offerings, whereas removed tiao are reduced to altars and open mounds — showing that the farther the generation, the more attenuated the ritual becomes.

sentences.zh: 若祧是文、武之廟，宜同月祭于太祖，雖推後稷以配天，由功德之所始，非尊崇之義每有差降也。

translations.literal: If the tiao were the temples of Wen and Wu, they ought likewise to receive monthly sacrifice with the Great Ancestor; although Hou Ji was elevated to match Heaven, that was because merit and virtue began with him, not because the meaning of honor admits no gradation.
translations.idiomatic: If the tiao were the temples of Wen and Wu, they ought to receive monthly sacrifice together with the Great Ancestor; although Hou Ji was elevated to match Heaven, that was because merit began with him, not because the principle of honor allows no gradation.

sentences.zh: 又禮有以多貴者，故傳稱德厚者流光，德薄者流卑。

translations.literal: Again, ritual has the principle that abundance confers honor; therefore the tradition says that thick virtue casts its light far, while thin virtue casts it low.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual also holds that greater merit confers greater honor; hence the tradition says that abundant virtue casts its radiance far, while meager virtue casts it low.

sentences.zh: 又雲自上以下，降殺以兩，禮也。

translations.literal: It also says that from above to below, diminution proceeds by twos — such is ritual.
translations.idiomatic: It also says that from higher to lower ranks, ritual diminishes by steps of two.

sentences.zh: 此則尊卑等級之典，上下殊異之文。

translations.literal: This is the canon of noble and base ranks and the text of distinction between higher and lower.
translations.idiomatic: This is the canon governing rank and precedence, the written rule distinguishing higher from lower.

sentences.zh: 而雲天子諸侯俱祭五廟，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet it says that Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike sacrifice at five temples — how so?
translations.idiomatic: Yet how can it be said that the Son of Heaven and the feudal lords alike sacrifice at five temples?

sentences.zh: 又王祭嫡殤，下及來孫，而上祀之禮，不過高祖。

translations.literal: Again, the king sacrifices for legitimate heirs who died young, extending down to remote descendants, yet the rite of ascending sacrifice goes no higher than the great-grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the king may sacrifice for legitimate heirs who died young, extending down to remote descendants, yet the rite of ascending sacrifice goes no higher than the great-grandfather.

sentences.zh: 推隆恩於下流，替誠敬於尊屬，亦非聖人制禮之意也。

translations.literal: To extend exalted favor downstream while displacing sincere reverence for honored kin is also not the intent of the sages in establishing ritual.
translations.idiomatic: To extend lavish favor downward while displacing sincere reverence owed to honored forebears is not what the sages intended when they established ritual.

sentences.zh: 是以泰始建廟，從王氏議，以禮父為士，子為天子諸侯，祭以天子諸侯，其屍服以士服。

translations.literal: Therefore when the Taishi temples were established, Wang's proposal was followed: by ritual the father was a common officer and the son became Son of Heaven or feudal lord; sacrifice was offered as to Son of Heaven or feudal lord, but the impersonator's garment was the officer's robe.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, when the Taishi temples were established, Wang's proposal was adopted: by ritual the father had been a common officer while the son became Son of Heaven or feudal lord; sacrifice was performed with royal rites, but the impersonator wore an officer's garment.

sentences.zh: 故上及征西，以備六世之數，宣皇雖為太祖，尚在子孫之位，至於殷祭之日，未申東向之禮，所謂子雖齊聖，不先父食者矣。

translations.literal: Thus sacrifice extended up to the Western Campaign lord to complete the count of six generations; although Emperor Xuan was the Great Ancestor, he still stood in the place of a descendant, and on the day of the great seasonal sacrifice the rite of facing east had not yet been performed for him — what is called 'though the son be equal to a sage, he does not take precedence over his father in eating.'
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice therefore extended up to the Western Campaign lord to complete six generations; although Emperor Xuan was the Great Ancestor, he still occupied the position of a descendant, and on the day of the great seasonal sacrifice the rite of facing east had not yet been accorded him — illustrating the rule that even a sage son does not take precedence over his father at the offering.

sentences.zh: 今京兆以上既遷，太祖始得居正，議者以昭穆未足，欲屈太祖于卑坐，臣以為非禮典之旨。

translations.literal: Now that those above Jingzhao have been moved, the Great Ancestor can at last take the central place; debaters, holding that the zhao and mu are not yet complete, wish to place the Great Ancestor in a lower seat — I hold that this is not the intent of the ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the shrines above Jingzhao have been moved, the Great Ancestor can at last take the central position; some debaters, believing the zhao and mu are not yet complete, wish to place the Great Ancestor in a lower seat — I hold that this violates the intent of the ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 所與太祖而七，自是昭穆既足，太祖在六世之外，非為須滿七廟，乃得居太祖也。

translations.literal: 'With the Great Ancestor, seven' means that the zhao and mu are already complete; the Great Ancestor stands beyond the sixth generation — it is not that one must fill seven temples before he may occupy the place of Great Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: 'Seven temples with the Great Ancestor' means that the zhao and mu are already complete; the Great Ancestor stands beyond the sixth generation — he does not need seven temples to be filled before he may take the position of Great Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 議者又以四府君神主宜永同于殷祫，臣又以為不然。

translations.literal: The debaters also held that the spirit tablets of the four lords ought forever to share the great seasonal sacrifice — I again held that this was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The debaters also argued that the spirit tablets of the four lords ought forever to share the great seasonal sacrifice — I again held that this was wrong.

sentences.zh: 傳所謂毀廟之主，陳乎太祖，謂太祖以下先君之主也。

translations.literal: What the tradition calls 'the tablets of abolished temples displayed before the Great Ancestor' means the tablets of former lords below the Great Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: What the tradition calls 'the tablets of abolished temples displayed before the Great Ancestor' refers to the tablets of former lords below the Great Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 故《白虎通》雲'禘祫祭遷廟者，以其繼君之體，持其統而不絕也。」

translations.literal: Therefore the Comprehensive Meaning says: 'The great seasonal sacrifices for moved temples are because they embody succession to the lordship and maintain the line without break.'
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Comprehensive Meaning states: 'The great seasonal sacrifices for moved temples are offered because those ancestors embodied succession to the lordship and preserved the line without break.'

sentences.zh: 豈如四府君在太祖之前乎。

translations.literal: How could the four lords stand before the Great Ancestor?
translations.idiomatic: How could the four lords stand before the Great Ancestor?

sentences.zh: 非繼統之主，無靈命之瑞，非王業之基，昔以世近而及，今則情禮已遠，而當長饗殷祫，永虛太祖之位，求之禮籍，未見其可。

translations.literal: They were not lords who succeeded to the line, bore no auspicious mandate of the spirits, and were not the foundation of royal enterprise; formerly they were included because the generation was near, but now sentiment and ritual are remote, yet they are to receive the great seasonal sacrifice forever and leave the Great Ancestor's place eternally vacant — sought in the ritual records, I do not see how this can be approved.
translations.idiomatic: They were not rulers who succeeded to the throne, bore no mandate confirmed by heavenly signs, and were not the foundation of the royal enterprise; they were included before only because the generations were near, but now feeling and ritual have grown remote, yet they are to receive the great seasonal sacrifice forever while the Great Ancestor's place remains empty — I find no approval for this in the ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 昔永和之初，大議斯禮，于時虞喜、范宣並以淵儒碩學，鹹謂四府君神主，無緣永存於百世。

translations.literal: In the beginning of the Yonghe era this ritual was debated at length; at that time Yu Xi and Fan Xuan, both profound scholars of vast learning, all held that the spirit tablets of the four lords had no reason to endure for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yonghe era this ritual was debated at length; Yu Xi and Fan Xuan, both profound and accomplished scholars, agreed that the spirit tablets of the four lords had no grounds to endure for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 或欲瘞之兩階，或欲藏之石室，或欲為之改築，雖所秉小異，而大歸是同。

translations.literal: Some wished to bury them between the steps, some to store them in the stone chamber, some to rebuild shrines for them; though their particular views differed slightly, the main conclusion was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed burying the tablets between the temple steps, others storing them in the stone chamber, others rebuilding shrines for them; though their particular proposals differed, they agreed in principle.

sentences.zh: 若宣皇既居群廟之上，而四主禘祫不已，則大晉殷祭，長無太祖之位矣。

translations.literal: If Emperor Xuan already stands above the mass of temples while the four lords continue in the great seasonal sacrifice without end, then in the great Jin seasonal rites the place of the Great Ancestor will forever be vacant.
translations.idiomatic: If Emperor Xuan already stands above the other temples while the four lords continue forever in the great seasonal sacrifice, then in Jin's great seasonal rites the Great Ancestor's place will remain permanently empty.

sentences.zh: 夫理貴有中，不必過厚；

translations.literal: Principle values hitting the mean and need not be excessive;
translations.idiomatic: Ritual principle values the mean and need not be excessive;

sentences.zh: 禮與世遷，豈可順而不斷！

translations.literal: ritual shifts with the age — how can one follow it without making a break!
translations.idiomatic: ritual changes with the times — how can one follow custom without ever drawing a line!

sentences.zh: 故臣子之情雖篤，而靈厲之諡彌彰；

translations.literal: Thus although the feeling of subject and son is deep, the posthumous title of the departed spirit grows ever more distinct;
translations.idiomatic: Thus although a subject's devotion may run deep, the posthumous title of the departed grows ever more distinct;

sentences.zh: 追遠之懷雖切，而遷毀之禮為用。

translations.literal: although longing to reach the remote past is keen, the rite of moving and abolishing temples is what applies.
translations.idiomatic: and although longing for the distant past may be intense, the rite of moving and abolishing temples is what must govern.

sentences.zh: 豈不有心于加厚，顧禮制不可逾爾。

translations.literal: Is it not that one has a mind to add still more honor, yet ritual institutions cannot be transgressed?
translations.idiomatic: It is not that the heart lacks desire to show greater honor, but ritual cannot be overstepped.

sentences.zh: 石室則藏於廟北，改築則未知所處，虞主所以依神，神移則有 瘞埋之禮。

translations.literal: The stone chamber lies north of the temple; rebuilding would leave the place unknown; the provisional tablet exists to lodge the spirit — when the spirit moves, there is the rite of burial.
translations.idiomatic: The stone chamber lies north of the temple; rebuilding would leave their resting place uncertain; the provisional tablet lodges the spirit, and when the spirit is transferred there is a rite of burial.

sentences.zh: 四主若饗祀宜廢，亦神之所不依也，准傍事例，宜同虞主之瘞埋。

translations.literal: If sacrifice to the four lords ought to be abolished, the spirits likewise have no lodging; following parallel precedents, they should be buried like provisional tablets.
translations.idiomatic: If sacrifice to the four lords ought to cease, their spirits likewise have no further lodging; following parallel precedents, their tablets should be buried as provisional tablets are.

sentences.zh: 然經典難詳，群言紛錯，非臣卑淺所能折中。」

translations.literal: Yet the classics are hard to detail fully and many opinions tangle and clash — this is not something my lowly shallowness can reconcile."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the classics are difficult to pin down and opinions conflict; this is more than my limited learning can reconcile."

sentences.zh: 時學者多從燾議，竟未施行。

translations.literal: At the time most scholars followed Dao's proposal, but in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: At the time most scholars sided with Dao, but in the end his proposal was not implemented.

sentences.zh: 遷通直郎，高祖鎮軍、車騎、中軍、太尉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant, and served as advisory aide to the Founding Emperor when he was General Who Guards the Army, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Central Army Commander, and Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Regular Attendant and served as advisory aide on the staffs of the Founding Emperor as General Who Guards the Army, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Central Army Commander, and Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 高祖北伐關、洛，大司馬琅邪王同行，除大司馬從事中郎，總留府事。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor marched north against Guan and Luo, the Prince of Langye, Grand Marshal, accompanied him; Dao was appointed attendant gentleman of the Grand Marshal and oversaw all affairs left at headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor marched north against Guanzhong and Luoyang, the Prince of Langye, serving as Grand Marshal, accompanied the campaign; Dao was appointed attendant gentleman on the Grand Marshal's staff and took charge of all affairs left behind at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 義熙十四年，除侍中。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yixi he was appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yixi he was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 元熙元年，以腳疾去職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxi he left office because of foot ailment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxi he resigned because of a foot ailment.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，征拜太常，雖外戚貴顯，而彌自沖約，茅屋蔬餐，不改其舊。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the mandate he was summoned and appointed Minister of Ceremonies; though a prominent maternal relative, he became only more self-restrained and modest, living in thatched huts on vegetable fare without changing his former ways.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor received the mandate, Dao was summoned as Minister of Ceremonies; though he was now a prominent imperial kinsman, he became only more restrained, keeping to his thatched dwelling and plain meals as before.

sentences.zh: 所得奉祿，與親戚共之。

translations.literal: The salary he received he shared with his kin.
translations.idiomatic: He shared his official salary with his relatives.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，致仕，拜光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he retired from office, was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and granted the golden seal and purple cord.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongchu he retired and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the golden seal and purple cord.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，時年七十。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died the same year, at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 少帝追贈左光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Emperor Shao posthumously awarded him Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and added the title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shao posthumously honored him as Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 長子邃，護軍司馬，宜都太守。

translations.literal: His eldest son Sui was marshal of the Protector Army and governor of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Sui served as marshal of the Protector Army and as governor of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 少子綽，太子中舍人，新安太守。

translations.literal: His younger son Chuo was attendant in the household of the Heir Apparent and governor of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Chuo served as attendant in the heir apparent's household and as governor of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 邃長子諶之，尚書都官郎，烏程令。

translations.literal: Sui's eldest son Chenzhi was a director in the Ministry of Justice and magistrate of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's eldest son Chenzhi served as a director in the Ministry of Justice and as magistrate of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 諶之弟凝之，學涉有當世才具，與司空徐湛之為異常之交。

translations.literal: Chenzhi's younger brother Ningzhi was broadly learned and possessed talent for the age; with Minister of Works Xu Tanzhi he formed an extraordinary friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Chenzhi's younger brother Ningzhi was widely learned and gifted for his age; he formed an unusually close friendship with Xu Tanzhi, Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 年少時與北地傅僧祐俱以通家子始為太祖所引見，時上與何尚之論鑄錢事，凝之便幹其語，上因回與論之。

translations.literal: In youth he and Fu Shengyou of Beidi, both sons of families linked by marriage, were first introduced to Emperor Taizu; at the time the emperor was discussing coinage with He Shangzhi, and Ningzhi at once joined their conversation, whereupon the emperor turned and debated with him.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he and Fu Shengyou of Beidi, both sons of allied families, were first presented to Emperor Taizu; when the emperor was discussing coinage with He Shangzhi, Ningzhi interjected, and the emperor turned to debate the matter with him.

sentences.zh: 僧祐引凝之衣令止，凝之大言謂僧祐曰：「明主難再遇，便應正盡所懷。」

translations.literal: Shengyou pulled Ningzhi's robe to make him stop; Ningzhi spoke loudly to Shengyou: "A clear-sighted lord is hard to meet twice — one ought at once to set forth fully what is in one's heart."
translations.idiomatic: Shengyou tugged at Ningzhi's robe to stop him, but Ningzhi said loudly: "A wise ruler is seldom met twice; one should speak one's mind fully while one can."

sentences.zh: 上與往復十餘反，凝之詞韻銓序，兼有理證，上甚賞焉。

translations.literal: The emperor and he went back and forth more than ten times; Ningzhi's phrasing was measured and orderly and combined reasoned proof — the emperor greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and he exchanged views more than ten times; Ningzhi's language was measured and orderly and supported by sound reasoning, and the emperor was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 曆隨王誕後軍記室錄事，欲以為青州，其事不果。

translations.literal: He successively served as recorder in the secretariat of Prince Dan of Sui's rear army, and there was a plan to make him regional inspector of Qingzhou, but the matter did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as recorder on the staff of Prince Dan of Sui's rear army; there was a plan to appoint him regional inspector of Qingzhou, but it did not come to pass.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞，以徐湛之党，為元兇所殺。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Assistant Director in the Secretariat and, as a partisan of Xu Tanzhi, was killed by the prime culprit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Assistant Director in the Secretariat and, as an associate of Xu Tanzhi, was executed by the prime culprit.

sentences.zh: 子夤，尚書主客郎，沈攸之征西功曹，為攸之盡節，事在《攸之傳》。

translations.literal: His son Yin was Master of Guests in the Secretariat and merit officer on Shen Youzhi's western campaign staff; he gave full loyalty to Youzhi — the affair is in the biography of Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin served as Master of Guests in the Secretariat and as merit officer on Shen Youzhi's western campaign staff; he gave his full loyalty to Youzhi, as recounted in Youzhi's biography.

sentences.zh: 凝之弟潭之，亦有美譽。

translations.literal: Ningzhi's younger brother Tanzhi also had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi's younger brother Tanzhi likewise enjoyed a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 太宗世，曆尚書吏部郎，禦史中丞。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Taizong he successively served as director in the Ministry of Personnel and as Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong he served successively as director in the Ministry of Personnel and as Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽中，為左民尚書，卒官。

translations.literal: Under the deposed emperor, in the Yuanhui era, he was Minister of the Left for the People and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Under the deposed emperor, during the Yuanhui era, he served as Minister of the Left for the People and died in office.

sentences.zh: 潭之弟澄之，太子左積弩將軍。

translations.literal: Tanzhi's younger brother Chengzhi was Left Master of Strong Crossbows in the Heir Apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi's younger brother Chengzhi served as Left Master of Strong Crossbows in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，領軍於盱眙，為索虜所破，見殺，追贈通直郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia he commanded troops at Xuyi, was defeated by the northern barbarians, and was killed; posthumously he was awarded Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia he commanded troops at Xuyi, was defeated by the northern invaders, and was killed; he was posthumously awarded the title Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 綽子煥，順帝升明中，為武昌太守。

translations.literal: Chuo's son Huan, in the Shengming era of Emperor Shun, was governor of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo's son Huan served as governor of Wuchang during the Shengming era of Emperor Shun.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之攻郢城，煥棄郡赴之；

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi attacked Yingcheng, Huan abandoned his commandery and went to join him;
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi attacked Yingcheng, Huan abandoned his post and went to join him;

sentences.zh: 攸之敗，伏誅。

translations.literal: when Youzhi was defeated, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: when Youzhi was defeated, Huan was executed.

sentences.zh: 傅僧祐，祖父弘仁，高祖外弟也。

translations.literal: Fu Shengyou — his grandfather Hongren was younger brother by marriage to the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shengyou's grandfather Hongren was the Founding Emperor's brother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 以中表曆顯官，征虜將軍、南譙太守，太常卿。

translations.literal: Through maternal kin ties he successively held eminent offices: General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, governor of Nanqiao, and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Through family connections he rose through prominent posts, serving as General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, governor of Nanqiao, and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 子邵，員外散騎侍郎，妻燾女也，生僧祐，有吏才，再為山陰令，甚有能名，末世令長莫及。

translations.literal: His son Shao was Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry; he married Dao's daughter and fathered Shengyou, who had talent for administration, twice served as magistrate of Shanyin with a great reputation for competence, and at the end of the dynasty no district magistrate could match him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shao served as Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, married Dao's daughter, and fathered Shengyou. Shengyou had a gift for administration, served twice as magistrate of Shanyin with great renown, and in the dynasty's final years no district magistrate could rival him.

sentences.zh: 亦以徐湛之党，為元兇所殺。

translations.literal: He too, as a partisan of Xu Tanzhi, was killed by the prime culprit.
translations.idiomatic: He too, as an associate of Xu Tanzhi, was executed by the prime culprit.

sentences.zh: 徐廣，字野民，東莞姑幕人也。

translations.literal: Xu Guang, styled Yemin, was a native of Gumu in Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang, whose courtesy name was Yemin, came from Gumu in Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 父藻，都水使者。

translations.literal: His father Zao was Commissioner of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zao served as Commissioner of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 兄邈，太子前衛率。

translations.literal: His elder brother Miao was Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Forward Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Miao served as Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Forward Guard.

sentences.zh: 家世好學，至廣尤精，百家數術，無不研覽。

translations.literal: His family for generations loved learning; Guang was especially accomplished, and among the hundred schools and numerological arts there was none he did not study.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long valued learning, and Guang surpassed them all, studying every branch of the hundred schools and the arts of calculation without exception.

sentences.zh: 謝玄為州，辟廣從事西曹。

translations.literal: When Xie Xuan was regional inspector, he summoned Guang as Western Bureau aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Xuan served as regional inspector, he recruited Guang as an aide in the Western Bureau.

sentences.zh: 又譙王司馬恬鎮北參軍。

translations.literal: He also served as northern campaign aide under Prince Qiao's staff officer Sima Tian.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as northern campaign aide on the staff of Sima Tian, staff officer to Prince Qiao.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝以廣博學，除為秘書郎，校書秘閣，增置職僚。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, because Guang was broadly learned, appointed him Secretary Gentleman to collate books in the Secret Archive and added staff positions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, recognizing Guang's erudition, appointed him Secretary Gentleman to collate books in the Secret Archive and expanded the staff.

sentences.zh: 轉員外散騎侍郎，領校書如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry and continued to head collation as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry while continuing to oversee collation as before.

sentences.zh: 隆安中，尚書令王珣舉為祠部郎。

translations.literal: In the Longan era, Minister of Works Wang Xun recommended him as Director of the Sacrifices Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longan era, Minister of Works Wang Xun recommended him as Director of the Sacrifices Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時會稽王世子元顯錄尚書，欲使百僚致敬，台內使廣立議，由是內外並執下官禮，廣常為愧恨焉。

translations.literal: At the time the heir of the Prince of Kuaiji, Yuanxian, controlled the Secretariat and wished all officials to pay him homage; within the capital Guang was made to draft the proposal, and thereafter inside and outside alike observed the rites of subordinate officers — Guang often felt shame and resentment over this.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuanxian, heir of the Prince of Kuaiji, controlled the Secretariat and wished all officials to pay him homage; Guang was ordered to draft the proposal within the capital, and thereafter officials inside and outside the court observed subordinate rites toward him — a matter that often filled Guang with shame and regret.

sentences.zh: 元顯引為中軍參軍，遷領軍長史。

translations.literal: Yuanxian brought him in as aide of the central army and promoted him to chief clerk of the Army of the Interior.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian recruited him as aide on the central army staff and later promoted him to chief clerk of the Army of the Interior.

sentences.zh: 桓玄輔政，以為大將軍文學祭酒。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan held power as regent, he appointed Guang libationer of letters on the Grand Marshal's staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan served as regent, he appointed Guang libationer of letters on the Grand Marshal's staff.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，高祖使撰車服儀注，乃除鎮軍諮議參軍，領記室。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi the Founding Emperor had him compile regulations for carriages, robes, and ceremonial observances, and appointed him advisory aide of the Army Who Guards the Army, heading the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yixi the Founding Emperor commissioned him to compile regulations for carriages, robes, and ceremonial protocol, and appointed him advisory aide on the Army Who Guards the Army staff, with charge of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 封樂成縣五等侯。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Lecheng county.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Lecheng county.

sentences.zh: 轉員外散騎常侍，領著作郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and headed the office of Master of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and appointed head of the Master of Writings office.

sentences.zh: 二年，尚書奏曰：「臣聞左史述言，右官書事，《乘》、《志》顯于晉、鄭，《陽秋》著乎魯史。

translations.literal: In the second year the Secretariat memorialized: "I have heard that the left historiographer records speech and the right official records affairs; the Cheng and Zhi were displayed in Jin and Zheng, and the Spring and Autumn Annals were set forth in Lu's chronicle.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the Secretariat memorialized: "We have heard that the left historiographer records speech and the right official records events; the Cheng and Zhi gained renown in Jin and Zheng, and the Spring and Autumn Annals were preserved in Lu's chronicle.

sentences.zh: 自皇代有造，中興晉祀，道風帝典，煥乎史策。

translations.literal: Since the imperial age was founded and Jin's sacrifices were restored, the way-wind and imperial canon shine brilliantly in the historical records.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the imperial house and the restoration of Jin's rites, the moral example of the imperial canon has shone brilliantly in the historical records.

sentences.zh: 而太和以降，世曆三朝，玄風聖跡，倏為疇古。

translations.literal: Yet from the Taihe era onward three reigns have passed, and the mysterious wind and sage traces have suddenly become antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the Taihe era onward three reigns have passed, and the sage's legacy has swiftly receded into the distant past.

sentences.zh: 臣等參詳，宜敕著作郎徐廣撰成國史。」

translations.literal: We your subjects have examined the matter and hold that Xu Guang, Master of Writings, should be ordered to complete the national history."
translations.idiomatic: We your subjects have reviewed the matter and submit that Xu Guang of the Master of Writings office should be ordered to complete the national history."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「先朝至德光被，未著方策，宜流風緬代，永貽將來者也。

translations.literal: The edict said: "The supreme virtue of the former court spread its radiance but was not recorded in the registers; its flowing influence should span generations and be bequeathed forever to those who come after.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "The supreme virtue of the former court spread its radiance yet was not recorded in the annals; its influence should span generations and be preserved for posterity.

sentences.zh: 便敕撰集。」

translations.literal: Let compilation be ordered at once."
translations.idiomatic: Let the compilation proceed at once."

sentences.zh: 六年，遷散騎常侍，又領徐州大中正，轉正員常侍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, also headed the great rectifier of Xu province, and was made full regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, also served as great rectifier of Xu province, and was later made a full regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 時有風雹為災，廣獻書高祖曰：「風雹變未必為災，古之聖賢輒懼而修己，所以興政化而隆德教也。

translations.literal: At the time wind and hail caused disaster; Guang submitted a letter to the Founding Emperor: "Wind and hail changes are not necessarily calamities; the sages of antiquity always feared them and cultivated themselves — thereby they raised government and exalted moral teaching.
translations.idiomatic: When wind and hail brought disaster, Guang wrote to the Founding Emperor: "Such omens are not necessarily calamities; the sages of antiquity always took them as warnings to refine themselves — and thereby raised good government and exalted moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 嘗忝服事，宿眷未忘，思竭塵露，率誠于習。

translations.literal: I once had the honor to serve you and have not forgotten your longstanding favor; I wish to exhaust the dust and dew of my strength and offer sincerity in what I have learned.
translations.idiomatic: I once had the honor to serve you and have not forgotten your kindness; I wish to offer whatever humble strength remains and speak with all sincerity from my experience.

sentences.zh: 明公初建義旗，匡複宗社，神武應運，信宿平夷。

translations.literal: When you first raised the righteous banner, restored the ancestral altars, and with divine martial prowess answered Heaven's mandate, peace was restored within a day or two.
translations.idiomatic: When you first raised the righteous banner and restored the ancestral altars, your divine martial prowess answered Heaven's mandate, and peace was restored within days.

sentences.zh: 且恭儉謙約，虛心匪懈，來蘇之化，功用若神。

translations.literal: Moreover you are respectful, frugal, modest, and restrained, humble in mind and never slack; the transformation of those who awaken from suffering works with godlike effect.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover you are respectful, frugal, and modest, never slack in self-cultivation; the relief you bring to the people works as if by divine power.

sentences.zh: 頃事故既多，刑德並用，戰功殷積，報敘難盡，萬機繁湊，固應難速，且小細煩密，群下多懼。

translations.literal: Recently affairs have multiplied, punishment and virtue are applied together, military merit has heaped up and rewards are hard to exhaust, and the myriad tasks are dense and pressing — naturally speed is difficult; moreover petty matters are intricate and many below are fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Recently affairs have multiplied, punishment and reward are applied together, military merit has piled up and rewards are hard to dispense, and the myriad tasks are pressing — swift action is naturally difficult; moreover petty matters are intricate and many subordinates live in fear.

sentences.zh: 又谷帛豐賤，而民情不勸；

translations.literal: Again, grain and cloth are abundant and cheap, yet the people's hearts are not encouraged;
translations.idiomatic: Grain and cloth are abundant and cheap, yet the people are not encouraged to prosper;

sentences.zh: 禁司互設，而劫盜多有，誠由俗弊未易整，而望深未易炳。

translations.literal: prohibitory offices are set up in mutual overlap, yet banditry is frequent — truly because popular abuses are not easily rectified and expectations run deep and are not easily made clear.
translations.idiomatic: prohibitory offices multiply upon one another, yet robbery remains common — truly because popular abuses are hard to correct and deep expectations are hard to satisfy at once.

sentences.zh: 追思義熙之始，如有不同，何者？

translations.literal: Reflecting on the beginning of Yixi, if there is something different, what is it?
translations.idiomatic: Looking back to the beginning of Yixi, if something has changed, what is it?

sentences.zh: 好安願逸，萬物之大趣，習舊駭新，凡識所不免。

translations.literal: Loving rest and wishing for ease is the great tendency of all things; being startled by the old when facing the new is what ordinary understanding cannot avoid.
translations.idiomatic: The love of ease is the great tendency of all things, and alarm at the new when accustomed to the old is what ordinary minds cannot avoid.

sentences.zh: 要當俯順群情，抑揚隨俗，則朝野歡泰，具瞻允康矣。

translations.literal: The essential thing is to bow to the feelings of the multitude and moderate and elevate according to custom — then court and countryside will rejoice in peace, and all who look up will find true tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: What matters is to heed the feelings of the people and adjust policy to custom — then court and countryside will rejoice in peace, and all who look to you will find true well-being.

sentences.zh: 言無可采，願矜其愚款之志。」

translations.literal: My words have nothing worth adopting; I only ask that you regard the sincerity of my foolish loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: My words may have little worth; I only ask that you regard the sincerity of my humble counsel."

sentences.zh: 又轉大司農，領著作郎皆如故。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Minister of Agriculture, continuing as before to head the Master of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Minister of Agriculture while continuing to head the Master of Writings as before.

sentences.zh: 十二年，《晉紀》成，凡四十六卷，表上之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Annals of Jin were completed, forty-six volumes in all, and were submitted in memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he completed the Annals of Jin in forty-six volumes and submitted them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，桓玄篡位，安帝出宮，廣陪列悲慟，哀動左右。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huan Xuan usurped the throne and Emperor An left the palace, Guang stood in attendance, grieved and sobbed, moving those on either side.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Huan Xuan usurped the throne and Emperor An was driven from the palace, Guang stood in attendance weeping so bitterly that he moved all those around him.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，恭帝遜位，廣又哀感，涕泗交流。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the abdication and Emperor Gong yielded the throne, Guang again was moved to grief, tears and mucus streaming down.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor accepted the abdication and Emperor Gong yielded the throne, Guang was again overcome with grief, tears streaming down his face.

sentences.zh: 謝晦見之，謂之曰：「徐公將無小過？」

translations.literal: Xie Hui saw this and said to him: "Master Xu, are you not being a little excessive?"
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui saw this and said to him: "Master Xu, are you not going a little too far?"

sentences.zh: 廣收淚答曰：「身與君不同。

translations.literal: Guang wiped away his tears and replied: "My person and yours are not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Guang wiped away his tears and replied: "My situation and yours are not the same.

sentences.zh: 君佐命興王，逢千載嘉運；

translations.literal: You assisted the mandate and raised the royal house, meeting a thousand-year auspicious fortune;
translations.idiomatic: You assisted the mandate and helped raise the new dynasty, meeting a once-in-a-millennium fortune;

sentences.zh: 身世荷晉德，實眷戀故主。」

translations.literal: my person and family received Jin's grace and truly cherish attachment to the former lord."
translations.idiomatic: my family and I received Jin's grace and truly remain attached to the former sovereign."

sentences.zh: 因更歔欷。

translations.literal: He then sobbed again.
translations.idiomatic: He then sobbed afresh.

sentences.zh: 傅隆，字伯祚，北地靈州人也。

translations.literal: Fu Long, styled Bozuo, was a native of Lingzhou in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Long, whose courtesy name was Bozuo, came from Lingzhou in Beidi.

sentences.zh: 高祖咸，晉司隸校尉。

translations.literal: His ancestor Xian was Metropolitan Commandant of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Xian served as Metropolitan Commandant under Jin.

sentences.zh: 曾祖晞，司徒屬。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xi was an attendant of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xi served as an attendant in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 父祖早亡。

translations.literal: His father and grandfather died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father and grandfather died while he was still young.

sentences.zh: 隆少孤，又無近屬，單貧有學行，不好交遊。

translations.literal: Long was orphaned in youth, had no close kin, was solitary and poor yet possessed learning and conduct, and did not care for socializing.
translations.idiomatic: Long was orphaned in youth, had no close relatives, and though poor possessed learning and integrity; he cared little for socializing.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，年四十，始為孟昶建威將軍，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi, aged forty, he first served Meng Chang as General Who Establishes Might and Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yixi, at the age of forty, he first entered service under Meng Chang as General Who Establishes Might and Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 坐辭兼，免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for declining a concurrent post.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for declining a concurrent appointment.

sentences.zh: 複為會稽征虜參軍。

translations.literal: He again served as aide on the campaign against the barbarians in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as aide on the Kuaiji campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 家在上虞，及東歸，便有終焉之志。

translations.literal: His family was in Shangyu; when he returned east he formed the wish to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: His family lived in Shangyu, and when he returned east he resolved to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 曆佐三軍，首尾八年。

translations.literal: He successively served on three army staffs for eight years in all.
translations.idiomatic: He served on three army staffs in succession for eight years altogether.

sentences.zh: 除給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射、丹陽尹徐羨之置建威府，以為錄事參軍，尋轉尚書祠部郎、丹陽丞，入為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi, Vice Minister of Works and governor of Danyang, established a Establishing Might headquarters and made Long recorder-aide; shortly he was transferred to Director of the Sacrifices Bureau in the Secretariat and assistant governor of Danyang, then entered as Left Assistant Director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi, Vice Minister of Works and governor of Danyang, established an Establishing Might headquarters and appointed Long recorder-aide; he was soon transferred to Director of the Sacrifices Bureau and assistant governor of Danyang, then entered the Secretariat as Left Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 以族弟亮為僕射，緦服不得相臨，徙太子率更令，廬陵王義真車騎諮議參軍，出補山陰令。

translations.literal: Because his clansman Liang was Vice Minister, as they were in the same mourning grade they could not face each other in office; he was moved to Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Rate Regulation, advisory aide on Prince Yizhen of Luling's chariots and cavalry staff, and went out to fill the post of magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Because his clansman Liang became Vice Minister, ritual mourning rules forbade them from serving together; Long was transferred to Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Rate Regulation, then advisory aide on Prince Yizhen of Luling's staff, and finally went out to serve as magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉初，除司徒右長史，遷禦史中丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia under Emperor Taizu he was appointed Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works and transferred to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanjia under Emperor Taizu he was appointed Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works and promoted to Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 當官而行，甚得司直之體。

translations.literal: He acted according to office and greatly embodied the integrity of the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He performed his duties with integrity and fully embodied the censor's role.

sentences.zh: 轉司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時會稽剡縣民黃初妻趙打息載妻王死亡，遇赦，王有父母及息男稱、息女葉，依法徙趙二千裏外。

translations.literal: At the time in Yan county of Kuaiji, Huang Chu's wife Zhao beat to death her stepson Zai's wife Wang; an amnesty was granted; Wang had parents and a son Cheng and daughter Ye by a former marriage; by law Zhao was to be banished two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: At the time in Yan county of Kuaiji, Huang Chu's wife Zhao beat her stepson Zai's wife Wang to death. Though an amnesty was granted, Wang had parents and children Cheng and Ye from a former marriage; by law Zhao was to be exiled two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 隆議之曰：「原夫禮律之興，蓋本之自然，求之情理，非從天墮，非從地出也。

translations.literal: Long submitted a deliberation: "Tracing the rise of ritual and law, it is rooted in what is natural and seeks what accords with reason — it did not fall from Heaven or spring from Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Long submitted a deliberation: "Ritual and law arise from what is natural and seek what accords with reason — they did not fall from Heaven or spring from Earth.

sentences.zh: 父子至親，分形同氣，稱之於載，即載之于趙，雖雲三世，為體猶一，未有能分之者也。

translations.literal: Father and son are the closest kin, sharing form and breath; as to Cheng, he is Zai's son and thus Zhao's grandson; though called three generations, in substance they are one — there is none who can divide them.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son are the closest of kin, sharing one flesh and breath; Cheng is Zai's son and thus Zhao's grandson; though called three generations, in substance they are one body — none can be divided from the rest.

sentences.zh: 稱雖創巨痛深，固無仇祖之義。

translations.literal: Though Cheng suffers wound beyond measure and pain beyond depth, there is fundamentally no principle of avenging a grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Though Cheng suffers wound beyond measure, there is no principle by which he may take vengeance on his grandmother.

sentences.zh: 若稱可以殺趙，趙當何以處載？

translations.literal: If Cheng may kill Zhao, how should Zhao treat Zai?
translations.idiomatic: If Cheng may kill Zhao, what is Zhao to do regarding Zai?

sentences.zh: 將父子孫祖，互相殘戮，懼非先王明罰，咎繇立法之本旨也。

translations.literal: Are father, son, grandson, and grandmother to slaughter one another in turn? I fear this is not the intent of the former kings in clarifying punishments or of Gao Yao in establishing law.
translations.idiomatic: Are father, son, grandson, and grandmother to slaughter one another in turn? I fear this is not what the former kings intended in clarifying punishments, nor what Gao Yao intended in establishing law.

sentences.zh: 向使石厚之子、日磾之孫，砥鋒挺鍔，不與二祖同戴天日，則石碏、秺侯何得流名百代，以為美談者哉！

translations.literal: Suppose the sons of Shi Hou and the grandsons of Rizhi had whetted blades and drawn swords and refused to live under the same sky as their two ancestors — how could Shi Que and the Marquis of Di have left their names for a hundred generations as subjects of fine renown!
translations.idiomatic: Suppose the sons of Shi Hou and the grandsons of Rizhi had drawn swords and refused to live under the same sky as their ancestors — how could Shi Que and the Marquis of Di have won praise for a hundred generations!

sentences.zh: 舊令雲，'殺人父母，徙之二千裏外'。

translations.literal: The old statute says: 'Those who kill another's parents are banished two thousand li.'
translations.idiomatic: The old statute states: 'Those who kill another's parents are banished two thousand li.'

sentences.zh: 不施父子孫祖明矣。

translations.literal: That it is not applied to father, son, grandson, and grandmother is clear.
translations.idiomatic: That it does not apply among father, son, grandson, and grandmother is clear.

sentences.zh: 趙當避王期功千里外耳。

translations.literal: Zhao need only avoid Wang's parents and those in the one-year mourning grade for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao need only keep a thousand li's distance from Wang's parents and close kin in mourning.

sentences.zh: 令亦雲，'凡流徙者，同籍親近欲相隨者，聽之'。

translations.literal: The statute also says: 'For all who are banished, if close kin of the same registry wish to follow, they are permitted.'
translations.idiomatic: The statute also states: 'For all who are banished, close kin of the same registry who wish to accompany them may do so.'

sentences.zh: 此又大通情體，因親以教愛者也。

translations.literal: This again greatly accords with human feeling and teaches love through kinship.
translations.idiomatic: This again accords with human feeling and teaches love through the bonds of kinship.

sentences.zh: 趙既流移，載為人子，何得不從；

translations.literal: Since Zhao is banished, Zai as her son — how can he fail to follow?
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhao is banished, how can Zai as her son fail to follow her;

sentences.zh: 載從而稱不行，豈名教所許？

translations.literal: if Zai follows and Cheng does not, is that permitted by the teaching of names?
translations.idiomatic: and if Zai follows while Cheng does not, is that permitted by moral teaching?

sentences.zh: 如此，稱、趙竟不可分。

translations.literal: Thus Cheng and Zhao ultimately cannot be separated.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Cheng and Zhao cannot ultimately be separated.

sentences.zh: 趙雖內愧終身，稱當沈痛沒齒，孫祖之義，自不得永絕，事理固然也。」

translations.literal: Though Zhao may feel inward shame all her life and Cheng bear deep grief to his grave, the bond of grandson and grandmother cannot be severed forever — such is the truth of the matter."
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhao may bear lifelong shame and Cheng lifelong grief, the bond between grandson and grandmother cannot be severed forever — such is the nature of the case."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: His proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 又出為義興太守，在郡有能名。

translations.literal: He again went out as governor of Yixing and in the commandery had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He was again sent out as governor of Yixing, where he earned a reputation for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 征拜左民尚書，坐正直受節假，對人未至，委出，白衣領職。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of the Left for the People; for integrity in accepting leave on festival days he left before the person he was to meet arrived and was dismissed, retaining office in plain robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Minister of the Left for the People; because on a festival leave he left before the person he was to meet arrived, he was dismissed but retained his post in plain robes.

sentences.zh: 尋轉太常。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 十四年，太祖以新撰《禮論》付隆使下意，隆上表曰：「臣以下愚，不涉師訓，孤陋閭閻，面牆靡識，謬蒙詢逮，愧懼流汗。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Emperor Taizu entrusted Long with the newly compiled Discourses on Rites to obtain his views; Long submitted a memorial: "I, being lowly and foolish, have not received teachers' instruction; solitary and crude in my lane, I face the wall without knowledge; wrongly receiving your inquiry, I am ashamed and fearful, sweating with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Emperor Taizu entrusted Long with the newly compiled Discourses on Rites to obtain his views; Long submitted a memorial: "I am lowly and unlearned, without teachers' guidance, ignorant and obscure; wrongly called upon for your inquiry, I am ashamed and fearful beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 原夫禮者，三千之本，人倫之至道。

translations.literal: Tracing it, ritual is the root of the three thousand norms and the utmost way of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual is the root of the three thousand norms and the highest way of human relations.

sentences.zh: 故用之家國，君臣以之尊，父子以之親；

translations.literal: Thus applied in state and family, lord and subject thereby gain honor, father and son thereby gain closeness;
translations.idiomatic: Applied in state and family, it lends honor to lord and subject and closeness to father and son;

sentences.zh: 用之婚冠，少長以之仁愛，夫妻以之義順；

translations.literal: applied in marriage and capping, young and old thereby gain loving kindness, husband and wife thereby gain righteous harmony;
translations.idiomatic: applied in marriage and capping rites, it fosters kindness between young and old and harmony between husband and wife;

sentences.zh: 用之鄉人，友朋以之三益，賓主以之敬讓。

translations.literal: applied among villagers, friends thereby gain the three benefits, host and guest thereby gain respect and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: applied among neighbors, it brings the three benefits to friendship and respect and yielding to host and guest.

sentences.zh: 所謂極乎天，播乎地，窮高遠，測深厚，莫尚於禮也。

translations.literal: What is called reaching to Heaven, spreading over Earth, exhausting height and distance, measuring depth and thickness — nothing is higher than ritual.
translations.idiomatic: What reaches to Heaven, spreads over Earth, exhausts height and distance, and measures depth and thickness — nothing surpasses ritual.

sentences.zh: 其樂之五聲，《易》之八象，《詩》之《風雅》，《書》之《典誥》，《春秋》之微婉勸懲，無不本乎禮而後立也。

translations.literal: The five tones of music, the eight trigrams of the Changes, the Feng and Ya of the Odes, the Canon and Announcements of the Documents, the subtle indirect admonition and warning of the Spring and Autumn Annals — none fails to be rooted in ritual before it is established.
translations.idiomatic: The five tones of music, the eight trigrams of the Changes, the Feng and Ya of the Odes, the Canon and Announcements of the Documents, and the subtle admonitions of the Spring and Autumn Annals — none is established except upon ritual as its foundation.

sentences.zh: 其源遠，其流廣，其體大，其義精，非夫睿哲大賢，孰能明乎此哉。

translations.literal: Its source is remote, its flow broad, its substance great, its meaning refined — unless one is a sage of penetrating wisdom, who can clarify this?
translations.idiomatic: Its source is remote, its flow broad, its substance great, and its meaning refined — who but a sage of penetrating wisdom can fully grasp it?

sentences.zh: 況遭暴秦焚亡，百不存一。

translations.literal: Moreover it suffered violent Qin's burning and destruction — not one part in a hundred survives.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, it suffered the burning destruction of brutal Qin, and scarcely one part in a hundred survives.

sentences.zh: 漢興，始徵召故老，搜集殘文，其體例紕繆，首尾脫落，難可詳論。

translations.literal: When Han arose, it first summoned old scholars and gathered surviving texts; their categories were tangled and beginnings and ends were lost — they are hard to discuss in detail.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arose, it summoned old scholars and gathered surviving texts, but the categories were tangled and passages were lost at beginning and end — they are hard to discuss in detail.

sentences.zh: 幸高堂生頗識舊義，諸儒各為章句之說，既明不獨達，所見不同，或師資相傳，共枝別幹。

translations.literal: Fortunately Gaotang Sheng knew something of the old meaning; the various scholars each made exegetical commentaries — clarity did not reach each alone, views differed, and teacher and pupil transmitted down separate branches from a common trunk.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately Gaotang Sheng preserved something of the old meaning; the various scholars each produced exegetical commentaries — clarity did not come to any one alone, views differed, and teacher and pupil transmitted separate branches from a common trunk.

sentences.zh: 故聞人、二戴，俱事後蒼，俄已分異；

translations.literal: Thus Wenren and the two Dai, all studying under Hou Cang, soon diverged;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Wenren and the two Dai all studied under Hou Cang, yet soon diverged;

sentences.zh: 盧植、鄭玄，偕學馬融，人各名象。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi and Zheng Xuan both studied under Ma Rong, each man naming his own symbols.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi and Zheng Xuan both studied under Ma Rong, yet each devised his own interpretive system.

sentences.zh: 又後之學者，未逮曩時，而問難星繁，充斥兼兩，摛文列錦，煥爛可觀。

translations.literal: Again, later scholars did not reach the former age, yet disputations multiplied like stars, filling more than two volumes, spreading texts and arraying brocade — brilliant and splendid to behold.
translations.idiomatic: Later scholars did not match their predecessors, yet disputations multiplied like stars, filling volume after volume with brilliant prose — splendid to behold.

sentences.zh: 然而五服之本或差，哀敬之制舛雜，國典未一于四海，家法參駁於縉紳，誠宜考詳遠慮，以定皇代之盛禮者也。

translations.literal: Yet the roots of the five grades of mourning garments sometimes err, the regulations of grief and reverence are mixed and confused, the national canon is not unified throughout the four seas, and family rules clash among the gentry — truly one should examine in detail with far-seeing thought to fix the great rites of the imperial age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the roots of the five mourning grades sometimes err, regulations of grief and reverence are confused, the national canon is not unified throughout the realm, and family rules clash among the gentry — truly we should examine these matters with far-seeing care to establish the great rites of the imperial age.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下欽明玄聖，同規唐、虞，疇咨四嶽，興言《三禮》，而伯夷未登，微臣竊位，所以大懼負乘，形神交惡者，無忘夙夜矣。

translations.literal: I bow my head — Your Majesty is reverent, bright, and mysteriously sage, matching Tang and Yu, consulting the four peaks and raising discourse on the Three Rites; yet Boyi has not yet ascended and I, a petty subject, usurp my post — therefore I greatly fear riding beyond my capacity and body and spirit alike are afflicted; I dare not forget vigilance day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is reverent, bright, and sage, matching the standards of Tang and Yu, consulting the four peaks and raising discourse on the Three Rites; yet the ritual masters have not yet taken their places while I, a petty official, hold my post unworthily — I greatly fear exceeding my capacity, and body and spirit alike are troubled; I dare not forget vigilance day and night.

sentences.zh: 而複猥充搏采之數，與聞爰發之求，實無以仰酬聖旨萬分之一。

translations.literal: Yet again I am unworthily counted among those who gather and collect, and have heard the request you have launched — truly I have no means to repay the imperial intent even one part in ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I am again unworthily counted among those who gather materials and have heard your request — truly I have no means to repay your intent even one part in ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 不敢廢默，謹率管穴所見五十二事上呈。

translations.literal: I dare not remain silent and waste words; respectfully I lead forth fifty-two matters seen through my tube-sized aperture and submit them above.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not remain silent; respectfully I submit fifty-two observations from my limited understanding.

sentences.zh: 蚩鄙茫浪，伏用竦赧。」

translations.literal: Ignorant, base, vast and confused, I prostrate myself and am seized with shame."
translations.idiomatic: Ignorant and confused as I am, I prostrate myself in shame."

sentences.zh: 明年，致仕，拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The next year he retired from office and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 歸老在家，手不釋卷，博學多通，特精《三禮》。

translations.literal: He returned in old age to his home, never letting books leave his hand; broadly learned and master of much, he was especially accomplished in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement at home he never laid aside his books; broadly learned and accomplished in many fields, he was especially expert in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 謹于奉公，常手抄書籍。

translations.literal: Diligent in public service, he often copied books by hand.
translations.idiomatic: Conscientious in public duty, he often copied books by hand.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，卒，時年八十三。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died, aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he died, at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：選賢於野，則治身業弘；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When worthies are selected in the countryside, then self-cultivation and enterprise are broad;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: When worthies are chosen from the countryside, self-cultivation flourishes;

sentences.zh: 求士子朝，則飾智風起。

translations.literal: when scholars are sought at court, then the fashion of displaying cleverness arises.
translations.idiomatic: when scholars are sought at court, the fashion of displaying cleverness takes hold.

sentences.zh: 《六經》奧遠，方軌之正路；

translations.literal: The Six Classics are profound and remote, the straight track and correct road;
translations.idiomatic: The Six Classics are profound and remote — the straight path and correct road;

sentences.zh: 百家淺末，捷至之偏道。

translations.literal: the hundred schools are shallow and marginal, the side path of quick arrival.
translations.idiomatic: the hundred schools are shallow and marginal — the shortcut and side path.

sentences.zh: 漢世登士，閭黨為先，崇本務學，不尚浮詭，然後可以俯拾青組，顧蔑籝金。

translations.literal: In Han, when men entered office, the village community came first; they honored the root and devoted themselves to learning, did not esteem empty trickery — only then could they stoop to pick up blue cords and look down on casket gold.
translations.idiomatic: In Han, advancement to office began with the local community; men honored fundamentals and devoted themselves to learning, scorning empty cleverness — only then could they win official rank with ease and disdain mere wealth.

sentences.zh: 於是人厲從師之志，家競專門之術，藝重當時，所居一旦成市，黌舍暫啟，著錄或至萬人。

translations.literal: Thus men sharpened the will to follow teachers, families competed in specialized arts, learning was weighty in the age — where one dwelt became a market in a day; when the schoolhouse briefly opened, those registered sometimes reached ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Thus men sharpened their resolve to follow teachers, families competed in specialized learning, and scholarship weighed heavily in the age — a master's dwelling could become a marketplace overnight, and when the academy opened, enrollment sometimes reached ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 是故仕以學成，身由義立。

translations.literal: Therefore office came through completion of learning, and the person was established through righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Thus office came through completed learning, and personal standing through moral principle.

sentences.zh: 自魏氏膺命，主愛雕蟲，家棄章句，人重異術。

translations.literal: From the time Wei received the mandate, lords loved ornamental writing, families abandoned exegetical clauses, and men prized strange arts.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Wei received the mandate, rulers loved ornamental prose, families abandoned classical exegesis, and men prized unorthodox arts.

sentences.zh: 又選賢進士，不本鄉閭，銓衡之寄，任歸台閣。

translations.literal: Again, in selecting worthies and advancing scholars, they did not take the village lane as root; the charge of the balance-scale was entrusted to the terrace offices.
