translations.idiomatic: Again, in selecting worthies and advancing scholars, local roots were ignored, and the power of evaluation passed to the central offices.

sentences.zh: 以一人之耳目，究山川之險情，賢否臆斷，萬不值一。

translations.literal: With one man's eyes and ears to investigate the perilous conditions of mountains and rivers, worth and unworth were judged by guesswork — not one in ten thousand was correct.
translations.idiomatic: With one man's eyes and ears to judge the conditions of every region, worth and unworth were decided by guesswork — scarcely one judgment in ten thousand was correct.

sentences.zh: 由是仕憑藉譽，學非為己，崇詭遇之巧速，鄙稅駕之遲難，士自此委笥植《經》，各從所務，早往晏退，以取世資。

translations.literal: Hence office relied on borrowed reputation, learning was not for oneself; they honored the clever speed of chance encounters and despised the slow difficulty of thorough mastery; scholars from this time set aside cases and planted the Classics, each following his own pursuit, going early and returning late to gain worldly capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hence office depended on borrowed reputation and learning was not pursued for its own sake; men honored quick cleverness and despised slow mastery; scholars set the Classics aside, each following his own pursuit, coming early and leaving late to gain worldly advantage.

sentences.zh: 庠序黌校之士，傳經聚徒之業，自黃初至於晉末，百餘年中，儒教盡矣。

translations.literal: The scholars of the schools and academies, the profession of transmitting the classics and gathering disciples — from Huangchu to the end of Jin, for more than a hundred years, Confucian teaching was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The scholars of the academies and the profession of transmitting the classics and gathering disciples — from Huangchu to the end of Jin, for more than a hundred years, Confucian teaching was exhausted.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，議創國學，宮車早晏，道未及行。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the mandate, there was discussion of founding a National Academy, but the imperial carriage departed early and the way had not yet been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor received the mandate, there was discussion of founding a National Academy, but he died before the plan could be carried out.

sentences.zh: 迄於元嘉，甫獲克就，雅風盛烈，未及曩時，而濟濟焉，頗有前王之遺典。

translations.literal: By Yuanjia it was at last accomplished; elegant wind and flourishing splendor did not reach former times, yet in abundance there was much of the former kings' surviving canon.
translations.idiomatic: By Yuanjia it was at last accomplished; its elegant culture did not match former ages, yet in abundance it preserved much of the former kings' legacy.

sentences.zh: 天子鸞旗警蹕，清道而臨學館，儲後冕旒黼黻，北面而禮先師，後生所不嘗聞，黃發未之前睹，亦一代之盛也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven with imperial banners clearing the way came by the purified road to the academy; the heir in cap-strings and embroidered robes faced north to pay rites to the former master — what the young had never heard and the gray-haired had never before seen was also the splendor of an age.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, his procession clearing the way, came by the purified road to the academy; the heir apparent in full regalia faced north to honor the former master — what the young had never heard and the aged had never seen was truly the splendor of an age.

sentences.zh: 臧燾、徐廣、傅隆、裴松之、何承天、雷次宗，並服膺聖哲，不為雅俗推移，立名於世，宜矣。

translations.literal: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, Fu Long, Pei Songzhi, He Chengtian, and Lei Cizong all embraced the sage and wise in their hearts, were not shifted by elegant fashion or vulgar custom, and established names in the world — as was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, Fu Long, Pei Songzhi, He Chengtian, and Lei Cizong all devoted themselves to the sages, were not swayed by fashion, and won renown in their age — as was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 潁川庾蔚之、雁門周野王、汝南周王子、河內向琰、會稽賀道養，皆托志經書，見稱於後學。

translations.literal: Yu Weizhi of Yingchuan, Zhou Yewang of Yanmen, Zhou Wangzi of Runan, Xiang Yan of Henei, and He Daoyang of Kuaiji all entrusted their aims to the classics and were praised by later students.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Weizhi of Yingchuan, Zhou Yewang of Yanmen, Zhou Wangzi of Runan, Xiang Yan of Henei, and He Daoyang of Kuaiji all devoted themselves to the classics and were praised by later scholars.

sentences.zh: 蔚之略解《禮記》，並注賀循《喪服》，行於世雲。

translations.literal: Weizhi had a partial understanding of the Record of Rites and also annotated He Xun's Mourning Garments, which circulated in the world, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhi had a partial understanding of the Record of Rites and also annotated He Xun's Mourning Garments, which circulated in his day.
